chapterTitle: Chapter 1: Periodic Classification of Elements and Periodicity
title: Chapter 1: Periodic Classification of Elements and Periodicity
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: According to the Modern Periodic Law formulated by Henry Moseley, the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their:
questions.explanation: Moseley showed using X-ray characteristic spectra that atomic number (nuclear charge Z) is the fundamental property determining an element's chemical nature.

questions.question: Which of the following electronic configurations represents an element belonging to the d-block of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s² (Iron, Fe) has its differentiating electron entering the penultimate 3d subshell, characterizing it as a d-block transition element.

questions.question: Along a period from left to right across the periodic table, atomic radius generally decreases primarily due to:

options.C: Increase in effective nuclear charge (Z_eff) while principal quantum number remains constant

questions.explanation: Electrons are added to the same valence shell while nuclear protons increase, pulling valence electrons closer to the nucleus.

questions.question: The steady decrease in ionic radii of trivalent lanthanide cations from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺ is known as:
questions.explanation: Poor shielding offered by diffuse 4f electrons causes the effective nuclear charge to pull valence electrons tighter, causing lanthanide contraction.

questions.question: Which of the following elements exhibits the highest first ionization energy?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest nuclear charge among Period 2 reactive nonmetals with a small atomic radius, requiring the most energy to remove an electron.

questions.question: Nitrogen has a higher first ionization energy than oxygen (1402 kJ/mol vs 1314 kJ/mol) because:

options.A: Nitrogen has a higher electronegativity than oxygen
options.B: Nitrogen possesses a stable half-filled 2p³ valence subshell
options.C: Oxygen has fewer electrons than nitrogen

questions.explanation: Half-filled subshells (2p³) possess extra exchange energy stability. Removing an electron from oxygen's paired 2p⁴ configuration relieves inter-electronic repulsion.

questions.question: Why does Chlorine have a more negative (higher) electron affinity (-349 kJ/mol) than Fluorine (-328 kJ/mol)?

options.A: Fluorine has lower electronegativity than Chlorine
options.B: Fluorine's compact 2p subshell creates high electron-electron repulsion that resists incoming electrons
options.C: Chlorine has vacant d-orbitals unavailable in Fluorine
options.D: Chlorine has smaller atomic radius than Fluorine

questions.explanation: Fluorine's tiny 2p subshell has exceptionally high electron density; incoming electrons experience strong repulsions, releasing less net energy than Chlorine's roomier 3p subshell.

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element with a Pauling value of 4.0.

questions.question: Hydration energy of metal cations depends on charge density. Which of the following cations has the greatest negative hydration enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Hydration energy is directly proportional to charge and inversely proportional to radius (charge density: q/r). Al³⁺ has +3 charge and small radius.

questions.question: Which of the following Period 3 oxides is amphoteric in nature?
questions.explanation: Al₂O₃ reacts with both acids (forming Al³⁺ salts) and strong bases (forming aluminate [Al(OH)₄]⁻), proving its amphoteric character.

questions.question: The melting and boiling points of elements in Period 2 and Period 3 reach a maximum at:
questions.explanation: Group IVA elements (C in diamond, Si) form giant covalent network lattices with four strong covalent bonds per atom, demanding enormous energy to melt.

questions.question: Which of the following hydrides is ionic (saline) in nature?
questions.explanation: NaH consists of Na⁺ and H⁻ ions in a crystalline ionic lattice, liberating H₂ gas at the anode upon electrolysis of its molten state.

questions.question: The diagonal relationship in the periodic table is exhibited between which pair of elements?
questions.explanation: Beryllium and Aluminum have remarkably similar charge-to-size ratios (charge density), leading to similar amphoteric oxides, covalent chlorides, and passivity with HNO₃.

questions.question: Which period of the periodic table is the shortest, containing only 2 elements?
questions.explanation: Period 1 contains only Hydrogen (1s¹) and Helium (1s²).

questions.question: The maximum oxidation state exhibited by an element is generally equal to its group number. Which transition element exhibits the maximum oxidation state of +7?
questions.explanation: Manganese ([Ar] 3d⁵ 4s²) utilizes all 7 valence electrons in compounds like KMnO₄ and Mn₂O₇ to show +7 oxidation state.

questions.question: Why does the second electron affinity of oxygen have a positive value (+780 kJ/mol) while the first is negative (-141 kJ/mol)?

options.A: The second electron is added to an already negatively charged O⁻ ion, requiring energy to overcome electrostatic repulsion
options.B: Oxygen becomes a noble gas after first electron addition
options.C: The valence shell expands to d-orbitals

questions.explanation: Adding an electron to a uninegative ion (O⁻) involves strong electrostatic repulsion, making the process endothermic (positive ΔH).

questions.question: Which of the following chlorides undergoes complete hydrolysis in water to produce an acidic solution and fumes of HCl?
questions.explanation: SiCl₄ possesses vacant 3d orbitals to accept lone pairs from water molecules, hydrolyzing violently to Si(OH)₄ and 4 HCl (unlike CCl₄ which lacks d-orbitals).

questions.question: The shielding effect of inner electrons across a period from left to right:
questions.explanation: Across a period, electrons enter the same principal quantum shell; the number of inner shielding core electron shells remains unchanged.

questions.question: Which Group IA element has the lowest density, actually floating on water?
questions.explanation: Lithium is the lightest solid metal with a density of only 0.534 g/cm³, easily floating on water.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is the most ionic halide of Period 3?
questions.explanation: NaCl has the greatest electronegativity difference (3.0 - 0.9 = 2.1) among Period 3 chlorides, forming a classic face-centered cubic ionic crystal.

questions.question: The tendency of heavier p-block elements (like Tl, Pb, Bi) to show stable oxidation states two units lower than their group valency is known as:
questions.explanation: The reluctance of outer ns² electrons to participate in bonding due to poor shielding of 4f/5d electrons is termed the inert pair effect.

questions.question: The acidic strength of normal oxides across Period 3 (Na₂O to Cl₂O₇):

options.B: Increases steadily from strongly basic to strongly acidic

questions.explanation: Na₂O and MgO are basic, Al₂O₃ is amphoteric, SiO₂ is weakly acidic, P₄O₁₀ and SO₃ are acidic, and Cl₂O₇ is strongly acidic.

questions.question: What is the total number of elements present in Period 4 of the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Period 4 fills 4s (2), 3d (10), and 4p (6) subshells, containing 18 elements from Potassium (Z=19) to Krypton (Z=36).

questions.question: Which of the following ions has the smallest ionic radius?
questions.explanation: These are isoelectronic species (10 electrons). Mg²⁺ has the highest nuclear charge (Z=12), pulling electrons closest to the nucleus.

questions.question: In which block of the periodic table are non-metals exclusively located (excluding Hydrogen and Helium)?
questions.explanation: All non-metals (C, N, O, P, S, Se, halogens, noble gases) reside in the p-block.

questions.question: An element with electronic configuration [Ne] 3s² 3p⁴ belongs to which group and period?
questions.explanation: Principal quantum number n=3 defines Period 3; valence electrons = 2 + 4 = 6, placing it in Group VIA (Sulfur).

questions.question: Which factor causes the atomic radius of noble gases to appear larger than the preceding halogen in experimental tables?

options.B: Their radii are measured as van der Waals radii rather than covalent radii

questions.explanation: Noble gases do not form stable covalent bonds at room temperature; their radii are recorded as van der Waals radii, which are inherently larger than bonded covalent radii.

questions.question: The basic character of alkali metal hydroxides down Group IA (LiOH to CsOH):

options.B: Increases because cation radius increases and lattice energy decreases, releasing OH⁻ ions more readily

questions.explanation: Larger cations down Group IA hold OH⁻ less tightly due to weaker electrostatic attraction, making CsOH the strongest base.

questions.question: Which of the following bonds has the highest percentage of ionic character?
questions.explanation: Cs-F combines the least electronegative metal (Cs = 0.79) and most electronegative nonmetal (F = 4.0), giving ΔEN = 3.21 and >92% ionic character.

questions.question: Elements belonging to the f-block are collectively designated as:
questions.explanation: Lanthanides and actinides have electrons filling the antipenultimate (n-2)f subshells, known as inner transition elements.

questions.question: Why is Beryllium fluoride (BeF₂) soluble in water while Barium sulfate (BaSO₄) is insoluble?

options.A: Be²⁺ has an exceptionally high hydration enthalpy exceeding its lattice energy
options.B: Ba²⁺ has higher hydration enthalpy than Be²⁺
options.C: BeF₂ is a giant covalent network

questions.explanation: Tiny Be²⁺ has immense charge density, resulting in hydration enthalpy so large that it easily overcomes lattice energy, dissolving BeF₂.

questions.question: Which element in the periodic table has the highest electrical and thermal conductivity at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Silver possesses the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of all known elements.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs represents isoelectronic ions?
questions.explanation: Both K⁺ (19 - 1 = 18) and Cl⁻ (17 + 1 = 18) possess 18 electrons (argon configuration).

questions.question: What is the general valence electronic configuration of Group IIIA (Group 13) elements?
questions.explanation: Group 13 elements (B, Al, Ga, In, Tl) possess ns² np¹ valence electron configuration.

questions.question: Mendeleev's original periodic table had several anomalies that were resolved by Moseley's atomic number arrangement, including the positioning of:
questions.explanation: Mendeleev placed Argon before Potassium based on chemical properties despite Argon having a higher atomic weight. Moseley's atomic number order (Ar=18, K=19) justified this placement.
